_case: UNANCHORED, and the hard end of the range. A Digi XBee 3 module soldered onto a populated PCB -- no bag, no distributor label, nothing but the part's own top marking. This is the case ADR 0021 exists for and the one CLAUDE.md rates at 30-60% end to end, and the limit is the marking-to-part lookup rather than the optics.
_why_this_case_is_worth_more_than_the_ot: Three of the four long alphanumeric strings on this label are NOT the part number, and all three are more prominently formatted than the one that is. A model that reads every character perfectly can still return the wrong string. That is the failure mode worth measuring, and a corpus of clean distributor bags would never surface it.
_identity_note: Printed as 'XB3-24Z8UM   rev F', rotated 90 degrees with the rest of the label. Decodes as XBee 3 (XB3), 2.4 GHz (24), Zigbee (Z), 8 = U.FL antenna, U = micro form factor, M = through-hole/SMT micro. 'MODEL: MICRO' on the line above corroborates the form factor.
_expected_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE. This case measures IDENTITY, not parameters: the module's electrical characteristics are nowhere on the label, so any parametric truth here would have to come from a datasheet nobody has fetched. Scoring extraction against it would be scoring a datasheet that was never read.
_distractor_note: Every one of these is printed on the label in the same block as the real part number, and each is a distinct way to be wrong. MCQ-XBEE3 is the FCC ID and 1846A-XBEE3 the Canadian IC certification number -- both contain the string 'XBEE3' and both look far more like a part number than XB3-24Z8UM does. 0013A2004 is Digi's OUI prefix (the top half of the module's MAC address). A8FB0200000002712 is the unit serial. 187ABE1 is the lower half of the MAC. A model returning any of these read the image correctly and misunderstood what it was looking at, which is a prompt problem; a model returning something that appears nowhere on the label invented it, which is the failure the never-auto-accept rule exists for. The scorer keeps them apart.
_hazards: Rotated text (the whole label reads bottom-to-top), a small Data Matrix on a curved reflective label that may not decode at all, specular glare from the metal shield, and a blob of cured adhesive across the lower edge of the module.
